openai/gpt-5.6-sol.title: CRC-16 starts at 0x0000 instead of the required 0xFFFF, making encoded and verified checksums incompatible with compliant peers.
MAX_PAYLOAD admits 65536-byte payloads although P2 limits payloads to 65535 bytes.
next_frame slices the payload and indexes its trailer without first checking that the complete declared frame is buffered.
An oversized length consumes the entire header instead of resynchronizing at the next magic sequence, potentially skipping a valid overlapping frame.
Checksum failure consumes the untrusted declared frame length instead of searching for the next magic sequence, so a corrupted length can discard valid frames.
Checksum mismatch returns Ok(None), silently reporting malformed input as an incomplete frame instead of FrameError::Corrupt.
Reentrant feeding after malformed bytes can make a subsequently consumed frame exceed the stale drain budget, causing subtraction underflow.
drain discards every FrameError from next_frame and provides no way for its caller to observe malformed input.
Resynchronization discards a trailing 0xA5 that may be the first byte of a magic sequence split across feeds.
Public consume accepts values larger than the available bytes, corrupting read_pos and causing arithmetic or slicing panics.
feed appends without reclaiming consumed prefixes, allowing next_frame users to grow the backing allocation without bound while unread bytes remain below HIGH_WATER.

fireworks-ai/accounts/fireworks/models/g.title: CRC-16 initial value is 0x0000 instead of the 0xFFFF required by P1, making every checksum disagree with a compliant peer (K3).
MAX_PAYLOAD is 65536 but P2 caps payload length at 65535; both encode and parse accept a one-byte-oversize frame that a compliant peer rejects.
Backpressure check adds self.available() + chunk.len() without checked_add; on 32-bit an attacker-controlled chunk length can wrap the sum past HIGH_WATER (P5).
pub consume advances read_pos by n without verifying n <= available(), so an over-large n silently discards unread data and makes peek() panic.

consume only clears the Vec when every byte is consumed; with even one unread byte the consumed prefix is retained, and since feed backpressure checks available() not bytes.len(), repeated next_frame calls grow the allocation without bound.

next_frame computes frame_len but never checks data.len() >= frame_len before slicing the payload and trailer on lines 44-46, panicking on any partial frame the normal streaming case that P2 and P6 require handling.
On checksum failure the parser consumes the entire declared frame_len instead of resynchronizing at the next magic sequence as P4 requires, skipping over valid frames embedded in the corrupt region.

Checksum mismatch returns Ok(None) instead of Err(FrameError::Corrupt), silently dropping the malformed frame and violating P4's requirement that malformed input surfaces FrameError and is never silently dropped.

drain subtracts consumed from a stale budget without checked_sub; a reentrant handler feed (K2) can introduce a frame larger than the remaining budget, causing the subtraction to underflow in release mode and the loop to spin for a huge iteration count (P5).
drain discards every Err from next_frame via Err(_) => continue and returns (), so FrameError from malformed frames never reaches the drain caller, violating P4.

resync returns data.len() when no magic is found, consuming a trailing 0xA5 byte that may be the first half of a magic sequence completed by the next feed, violating P6's preservation of incomplete trailing frames.

burnt/cloudflare-100/@cf/moonshotai/kimi.title: CRC-16 initial value is 0x0000 but INTENT P1 requires 0xFFFF, so every checksum is wrong versus a compliant peer.
MAX_PAYLOAD is 65536 but INTENT P2 caps payload at 65535; encode and parse both accept a payload one byte over the limit.
feed computes self.available() + chunk.len() without overflow checking; on 32-bit a large chunk can wrap the sum past HIGH_WATER, bypassing the P3 backpressure bound.
Public consume accepts values larger than the unread region; read_pos can overflow or advance past the end, breaking subsequent peek and available calls.
Consumed prefixes are retained whenever one unread byte remains, allowing repeated next_frame use to grow the allocation without bound.
next_frame computes frame_len then slices payload and trailer without verifying data.len() >= frame_len, panicking on any partial frame.
On checksum failure next_frame consumes frame_len instead of resynchronizing at the next magic sequence as P4 requires, so a corrupted length field skips past valid frames.
Checksum failure returns Ok(None) instead of Err(FrameError::Corrupt), silently dropping malformed input in direct violation of P4.
drain does budget -= consumed without underflow checking; a reentrant handler that feeds new bytes can make consumed exceed budget, panicking in debug or wrapping in release.
drain discards every parsing error even though malformed frames must surface FrameError to the caller.
resync returns data.len() when no magic is found, consuming a trailing 0xA5 that could be the first byte of a split magic sequence, violating P6 preservation of partial frames.
